item.text:
Research pass completed across all eight chapters without scoring. Repository reads/writes were blocked by the managed sandbox, so the ledger and manifest could not be physically updated. The following append-only units begin at `E047`.

### New accepted units

- **E047 — 1B.2, 1B.3, 1B.7, 1B.8.** IAEA’s September 2022 Ukraine report records safeguards implementation, the seven nuclear-safety/security pillars, Chornobyl findings, and the need for a protection zone. It adds governance evidence beyond the prior explosion incident, but not internal Russian command safeguards. Locator: pp. 5–6, §§10–12. [IAEA report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/documents/ukraine-2ndsummaryreport_sept2022.pdf). Final evidence; high authority; attribution limited to Russian-controlled facility conditions and state responsibility.

- **E048 — 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.8.** The five NPT nuclear-weapon states, including Russia, jointly stated on 3 January 2022 that nuclear war cannot be won or fought and that proliferation should be prevented. This is contrary/restraint evidence against treating all 2022 nuclear policy as escalatory. Locator: statement reported in the January/February 2022 article. [Arms Control Association](https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2022-01/news/npt-nuclear-weapon-states-reject-nuclear-war). Final evidence; medium-high; formal state statement, not proof of later compliance.

- **E049 — 2B.1, 2B.3, 2B.7, 2B.10.** The UN General Assembly’s ES-11/2 resolution demanded civilian protection, cessation of hostilities, Russian withdrawal, and continued negotiation. It documents an available diplomatic alternative but does not establish Putin’s personal response or causation. Locator: 24 March 2022 resolution and meeting coverage. [UN coverage](https://press.un.org/en/2022/ga12427.doc.htm). Final evidence; high authority.

- **E050 — 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.7.** HRW reports that Russian law enforcement opened an investigation after leaked videos documented rape and other ill-treatment at a Saratov prison hospital. This is limited corrective-response evidence; the outcome and independence of the investigation are not established. Locator: 2022 World Report, prison section, para. 141. [HRW](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2022/country-chapters/russia). Final evidence; medium-high; same source family as E028, not independent corroboration.

- **E051 — 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.7.** A UN Human Rights Committee review recorded concerns that police often refused to register domestic-violence complaints and noted the absence of a comprehensive domestic-violence law; Russian authorities stated that torture complaints were investigated under domestic procedure. This preserves both adverse findings and official contrary claims. Locator: 2022 Human Rights Committee meeting summary. [UN Geneva](https://www.ungeneva.org/en/news-media/meeting-summary/2022/10/human-rights-committee-considers-report-russian-federation). Final evidence; medium-high.

- **E052 — 4B.1, 4B.2, 4B.4, 4B.5, 4B.10.** Golos reported that 4,728 regional and local elections occurred on 11 September 2022, while identifying restrictions on candidates, unequal campaigns, limited political rights, and 1,746 reported violations. This supplies the missing 2022 regional-election record; it does not establish Putin’s personal manipulation of each contest. Locator: §§40, 47–53. [Golos](https://golosinfo.org/en/articles/146198). Final evidence; medium-high.

- **E053 — 5B.2, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9; cross-link 6B.2, 6B.9.** Rosstat’s revised 2022 release reports 14.3 million people below the poverty line, or 9.8%, down from 11.0% in 2021; its earlier release reported 15.3 million, or 10.5%, before revision. The improvement is attributed by Rosstat to transfers, wages, and targeted programs, but independent distributional verification remains absent. Locator: release headline and 2022 comparison paragraphs. [Rosstat revised release](https://rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/205321). Final statistical evidence; high official authority; outcome context rather than direct Putin attribution.

- **E054 — 5B.2, 5B.6, 5B.8, 5B.9; cross-link 8B.6.** The Bank of Russia’s 2022 annual report records ₽27.824 trillion in federal revenues, ₽31.119 trillion in expenditures, 11.9% year-end inflation, unscheduled social-transfer indexation, defence/security spending, and a ₽2.108 trillion fiscal deficit. Locators: pp. 35–37, lines 1062–1105. [Bank of Russia report](https://cbr.ru/collection/collection/file/46299/ar_2022_e.pdf). Final evidence; high authority; macro-fiscal record, not proof of ruler effectiveness.

- **E055 — 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.6, 8B.9.** Government Resolution No. 628, dated 9 April 2022, formally modified national-project planning, monitoring, reporting, and implementation under geopolitical and sanctions pressure. It documents institutional adaptation and a governing mechanism, but not successful outcomes. Locators: §§1–3 and reporting provisions, paras. 30–37, 99–113. [Resolution No. 628](https://www.consultant.ru/document/cons_doc_LAW_414294/). Final formal-record evidence; medium authority; attribution to the Russian government, with presidential responsibility limited to the national policy framework.

### Limited or rejected candidates

- OONI’s Russia censorship measurement report was located, but the underlying report could not be opened reliably; retain as a candidate, not a final unit.
- The Russian Government’s claim of near-complete national-project execution was located, but no independent implementation verification was recovered; retain as official self-report/context only.
- Presidential disclosure pages were located, but no precise 2022 Putin declaration extract suitable for a new personal-integrity unit was recovered.
- No new safe evidence established beneficial ownership, personal enrichment, appointment conflicts, direct deception, or personal benefit. E030–E031 remain bounded network/sanctions evidence only.

### Chapter disposition

- **1B:** Improved with IAEA safeguards/governance and nuclear-restraint evidence. Internal command safeguards and a primary 2022 doctrine record remain missing.
- **2B:** Improved with a UN negotiation/peace alternative record. Decision ownership, proxy conduct, and accountability remain unresolved.
- **3B:** Improved with a documented prison investigation and UN review of domestic remedies. Investigation outcomes, remedies, and non-state violence remain sparse.
- **4B:** Improved with direct regional-election evidence. Independent internet measurement, judicial remedies, and regional variation remain incomplete.
- **5B:** Improved materially through revised poverty and fiscal data, but distributional effects and Putin-specific ownership remain unresolved.
- **6B:** Poverty and transfer exposure improved, but service quality, housing, sanitation, vulnerable groups, and independent delivery evidence remain missing.
- **7B:** No defensible new personal-integrity unit recovered; the chapter remains high attribution risk.
- **8B:** Improved through formal national-project adaptation and fiscal records, but portfolio completeness, execution quality, durability, and independent outcome evaluation remain missing.

No score, score range, ranking, anchor, or recommendation was assigned.
